requirement:
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
rationale:
**Obligation.** `requirements.references.outline_selectors` has one obligation: Habeas uses the TBV outline selector grammar for source addresses. The grammar's own rules belong to the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`. I did not reassess that requirement's implementation or tests. I only checked that the subject's tests apply the grammar to the addresses Habeas produces and accepts.

**Mapping to tests.**
- **Generated selectors follow the grammar.**
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` checks `kind[name]` segments, nesting with `/`, percent-encoding (`impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`), `#N` disambiguation (`fn[repeated]#1` and `#2`), and the empty selector resolving to the root. It also checks that an ambiguous selector and a missing selector both fail.
  - `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` checks that anonymous nodes get `use@` plus 12 hex digits, that the selector survives insertions, that it stops resolving when the node changes, and that identical nodes get `#1` and `#2`.
  - `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` checks `line@` selectors. It asserts that identical lines share one selector that resolves, and that whitespace-only differences in a line leave its selector unchanged.
  - `anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits` checks the exact form `pair[items]/item@<first 12 hex digits of identity_hash>`. It checks that the selector survives an edit to a descendant and that a child path under it resolves.
  - `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` checks Markdown anonymous segments (`kind@` plus 12 characters) and that every generated selector resolves back to its own node.
- **Invalid and missing selectors.** `profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent` asserts that a well-formed but missing selector gives a not-found error. It also asserts that `fn[bad%ZZ]` gives `ResolveError::Invalid` with a "malformed percent escape" message.
- **Source addresses.** `outline_addresses_validate_selectors_without_reading_paths` covers the `OutlineData::new` boundary, where an address is built from a path and a selector.
  - It accepts `""`, `fn[kept]`, and a percent-encoded `mod[a%2Fb]/fn[kept]`, and checks they are kept verbatim.
  - It rejects `fn[missing`, `fn[bad%ZZ]`, and `/fn[kept]`.
- **Habeas consumers of the grammar.**
  - The impl sites `src/inputs.rs#impl[ParsedSource]/fn[resolve]` and `src/authoring/tools.rs#impl[SearchNodes]/fn[entries]` reuse the outline's resolve and its generated selectors.
  - `ParsedSource::resolve` only wraps `outline.resolve` and sorts the failure into invalid, ambiguous, or missing. `SearchNodes::entries` passes `node.selector` through unchanged. Neither has selector logic of its own.
  - Tests in `tests/evidence_boundaries.rs`, `fn[outline_inputs_survive_moves_and_unhashed_comments_but_not_edits]`, also assert the invalid and missing diagnostics. They belong to `requirements.ci.outline_inputs`, not to this requirement.

**Possible violations the tests would miss.** I found none that are plausible. If Habeas stopped using the shared grammar, for example by emitting line-number selectors or unencoded names, the generated-selector and round-trip assertions would fail. If address validation were loosened or tightened, the accept and reject cases in `outline_addresses_validate_selectors_without_reading_paths` would fail.

**Other points.** Every test has a {test} reference to the subject. I found no marking gap and no fixme acknowledgments, and I identified no ambiguity in the text.

text: An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
